subject: Clarifications on annotated dataflow, KMS responsibility, and subprocessor custody
messages:
From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@bluepeakhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy-ops@bluepeakhealth.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: annotated dataflow + KMS custody questions

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our DPA review and the SSQ intake, our security team asked for a version of your dataflow diagram with the following annotations: which components process or store PII, where pseudonymization happens, and which services have access to unredacted values. Separately, we need a clear statement on KMS responsibility: who manages, rotates, and can export customer keys (Redwood, dedicated subprocessor, or customer-managed).

Can you: 1) share an annotated diagram (preferably PNG or PDF), 2) confirm KMS custody model for both Redwood Hosted and Dedicated deployments, and 3) indicate which subprocessors (if any) have access to encryption keys or plaintext PII?

Target: we have an internal review on Friday (2026-08-06); if you can get a draft back by EOD Wed (8/4) that would be ideal.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Daniel Ruiz
Director, Privacy & Security
BluePeak Health

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@bluepeakhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: annotated dataflow + KMS custody questions

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide this. Quick answers up front:
- We'll attach an annotated dataflow (png) showing PII touchpoints and where pseudonymization happens.
- For Redwood Hosted (our public API), keys are managed by Redwood KMS; customers can request HSM-backed key wrapping for enterprise plans. No external subprocessor can export plaintext keys.
- For Dedicated, customers can choose customer-managed keys via a KMS integration (we support AWS KMS and Google Cloud KMS) and we can provide a hosted key-wrapping option if needed.
- Subprocessors: storage and logging backends are operated by our cloud provider partners; none have access to plaintext keys for hosted customers. For Dedicated with customer-managed keys, Redwood does not hold key material.

I'll circulate an internal draft annotated diagram and a KMS ownership table for you by EOD Wed. Looping in Marcus (infra) and Irene (security) for technical detail.

Would you like the annotated diagram to call out tokenization/pseudonymization at the request layer, or annotate the model inference path as well?

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Grace — this is great, thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of follow-ups from our security reviewers after an initial read:

1) For the ephemeral KV cache used during inference, can you confirm if any cache shards are persisted to object storage during autoscaling events? If so, how long are they retained and what encryption controls apply?

2) You mentioned 'no external subprocessor can export plaintext keys' — can you explicitly list the subprocessors (by name and role) that have any role in handling encrypted blobs vs. any opportunity to access unencrypted PII?

3) For Dedicated deployments where customers choose customer-managed keys, can you provide an example of the least-privilege IAM policy the customer should attach to their CMK to enable Redwood's runtime to decrypt/infer?

If you can include short examples and the requested list in the deliverable, that will help us close the SSQ quickly. Thanks — can you still target EOD Wed?

— Daniel
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@bluepeakhealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: annotated dataflow + KMS custody questions

Daniel — attaching the deliverables in advance of the full zip: annotated-dataflow-v2.png; kms-ownership-table.xlsx; ssq-responses-v0.3.docx. Summary answers inline below.

- KV cache persistence: we do not persist unencrypted KV cache shards to long-term object storage during autoscaling. Short-lived cache checkpoints (encrypted at rest with service-side keys) may be staged to ephemeral object storage for 5–15 minutes during scale operations; these are encrypted using provider-managed keys, and are deleted after autoscale completes. For Hosted customers we can provide an audit trail showing the short-lived object IDs and deletion timestamps on request.

- Subprocessors (brief):
  * GCP (storage & compute) — manages infrastructure; no access to plaintext PII (Redwood controls encryption keys for Hosted).
  * FastLog Inc. (metrics/logs vendor) — receives aggregated telemetry; no plaintext PII.
  * ModelCloudOps (inference partner for specialized hardware) — operates isolated runtime; cannot export keys; only sees pseudonymized request ids.

- Example least-privilege IAM for Dedicated (AWS KMS):
  Policy name: redwood-dedicated-kms-decrypt-role
  Allowed actions: kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext (restricted to specific key alias), kms:DescribeKey
  Resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/EXAMPLE-KEY-ID
  Condition: aws:SourceVpce or aws:SourceIp to restrict usage to Redwood-managed VPC endpoints

I'll also include Mina's audit log snippets in the assembled doc. Grace will send the Drive link to you in a separate email.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
